name: WiredTiger
tagline: MongoDB's default storage engine: MVCC B-tree with compression and snapshot isolation.
description: WiredTiger is a high-performance embeddable storage engine created by the authors of Berkeley DB and acquired by MongoDB in 2014; it has been MongoDB's default engine since 3.2. It provides row-store and column-store B-trees with document-level concurrency control, multi-version snapshot isolation, block compression, checkpoints plus a write-ahead log, and hooks for encryption. Development is driven by MongoDB's needs and it is now tagged alongside MongoDB server releases, with standalone releases last cut in 2024. It can be embedded directly, but the community outside MongoDB is small.

license.name: GNU GPL v2 or v3, or MongoDB commercial license

pricing.notes: GPL for open-source use; commercial licensing via MongoDB.

scale.notes: Single-process engine; scales to multi-TB per MongoDB node.

strengths: Document-level (record-level) concurrency with MVCC snapshot isolation
Block compression (snappy, zlib, zstd) and prefix compression
Timestamp-based reads that power MongoDB's majority reads and transactions
Row and column store formats in one engine
weaknesses: Roadmap is driven entirely by MongoDB
GPL license complicates embedding in proprietary products
Cache-pressure and eviction tuning can be tricky
useCases: Embedding a transactional engine in a custom C system
notIdealFor: Teams wanting a permissively licensed embeddable engine
Simple key-value needs (LMDB, RocksDB are easier)
